simple.meaning: סָבַךְ (çâbak) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to entwine.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Job, Nahum, beginning at Job 8:17. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סָבַךְ (H5440) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: סָבַךְ (çâbak) / H5440 is traced through Job 8:17, Nahum 1:10 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H5440. sabak [ סָבַךְ ] verb interweave (|| form to שׂבך q. v.); — Qal Passive participle plural סְבֻכִים סִירִים Nahum 1:10 interwoven (entangled) thorns (compare Da); Gunk ZAW xiii (1893), 235 proposes (after ᵑ7 ᵐ5 Vollers) כְּסוּחִים i.e. cut off, away ( Isa 33:12 ) compare Now; text very dubious Pu`al Imperfect 3masculine plural יְסֻבָּ֑כוּ שָׁרָשָׁיו עַלגַּֿל Job 8:17 are interwoven (in a tangled mass).

occurrences.englishText: His roots are wrapped around the rock pile.
For entangled like thorns, and drunken as with their drink, they are consumed utterly like dry stubble.
